rules.adoption: Adopted 14 Oct 2026 by the profile owner under Methodology v1.1. Drafted 2026-09-26 from the Dice and Keno profiles (dice 1.0.2-draft, keno 1.0.2-proposed).
rules.reproduction: Byte identity is required only for exact content. A pinned artifact's hash asserts the identity of the committed evidence — the dataset, the config, the seeds and the census (integer counts, round totals, integer-unit money) — and verify never rewrites it. A regeneration is written to outputs/run/ and compared with the committed artifact field by field: integers and strings exact; non-integer numbers within |Δ| ≤ 1e-14 + 1e-12·max(|a|,|b|), or the per-field tolerance a step declares; the diff records the runtime version and must be empty beyond tolerance. Run metadata is absent, not excluded. No verdict-bearing comparison turns on a difference below its declared tolerance. Shared with the Plinko, Dice, Mines and Keno profiles (rules.reproduction).
rules.applicability: A check applies unless its `applies` predicate over the declaration is false. The engine evaluates the predicate; a false result prints the step as n/a with the derived reason (path, declared value) and the declared value is verified against the dataset or pinned config by the rule in `declarationTruth` (conformance C-13). A declaration never asserts n/a directly; `notApplicable` lists are ignored from 1.0.2. Keno/Limbo addition: a declared null means the package does not establish the fact (listed in the declaration's `unknowns`); a null never evaluates an `applies` predicate to false — the check stands. Only a measured false / 0 / null-by-design (e.g. money.balanceField) derives n/a.
rules.drawBias: R1 (carried from DICE-08): the draw is exactly uniform or biased ≤ 2^-32, stated as a computed bound — rejection sampling: maxFair + census; a direct uint32 with no range reduction: bound 0 by construction; float draw: the float→result mapping enumerated and the per-target win-probability deviation printed with its RTP effect.
rules.maxPayout: R2 (carried from DICE-14 / MINES-14): every served multiplier lies within the declared caps; a violation is disclosed, not failed. Limbo extends it to the target bounds, the result cap, the exposure / max-payout clip and an advertised maximum target no legal stake can play (LIMBO-14).
rules.edgeClaim: Limbo addition (LIMBO-19): an edge claim is a claim about every legal target, so it is compared with the edge derived for the whole target grid, not with the targets a capture happened to use. A deviation already disclosed with its magnitude but not FLAGged is recorded as partial, not implemented. The FLAG follows the RTP-CLAIM band — only a target more than the band from the claim, on the range the rule scores, is flagged; inside the band the edge curve is printed in full (min / max / where / count off the claim).
rules.phaseLabels: The elevated-stake run is labelled Phase C and the player-seed run Phase D (read from the dataset’s phase labels), so LIMBO-06 and LIMBO-12 are read by letter.

numbering: Shared with the Plinko, Dice, Mines, Blackjack and Keno profiles: LIMBO-nn is the same property as DICE-nn / KENO-nn for the 24 core checks; slots 10, 13, 14, 15, 17 and 19 are game-specific; LIMBO-31 (scaling edge, the Limbo form of KENO-31 / PLINKO-39) is an addition.

policies.HARD_FAIL: any violation → NOT PROVABLY FAIR; verify exits 1
policies.FLAG: violation is disclosed with a limitation row; verify exits 2. A FLAG carries an origin: operator (the residual is about the game → Conditional Pass) or capture (an auditor-side artefact such as a capture retry → limitation row, verdict class unchanged). Decided 2026-09-17.
policies.INFORMATIONAL: reported with its statistic and its reading, never affects the verdict and is never counted as a flag, whatever the statistic says; verify's exit code does not depend on it. The live-sample fit (check 22) is informational everywhere.
policies.RELEASE_GATE: package check that blocks publication when it fails; it never changes the verdict
policies.GRADED: not verdict-bearing; scored 1–5 in the QA scorecard and gated at release by the conformance floor

statusLegend.implemented: the check exists as specified and uses the declared parameters
statusLegend.partial: the check exists but is weaker than the profile (what is missing is stated)
statusLegend.missing: no step or package item covers it
statusLegend.n/a-declared: the casino's design makes it inapplicable; the declaration says why and the step prints it

checks.name: Seed hash integrity
checks.asserts: Every revealed server seed hashes to its published commitment under the declared encoding; the number of seeds checked equals the code constant for the audited population, not a count read from the dataset.

checks.name: Forward commitment chain
checks.asserts: For every rotation, the next-seed hash published before the rotation equals the active hash after it, and a pre-capture link anchors the chain before epoch 0. Recomputed from raw fields, never from a capture-script boolean.
checks.floor: All rotation events — zero unverified transitions
checks.declarationTruth: no key matching /next.*hash/i on any epoch record when declared null

checks.name: Hash consistency within epoch
checks.asserts: All bets sharing an epoch carry the same server-seed hash and the same client seed.

checks.name: Nonce continuity
checks.asserts: Within every epoch the nonces are exactly base … base+epochSize−1 with no gap, repeat or reorder. An operator-side gap or repeat is a HARD FAIL. A gap the capture log attributes to an auditor-side retry is a FLAG with origin = capture: counted, given a limitation row, never a PASS — and it does not change the verdict class (decided 2026-09-17).
checks.floor: Nonce gap or repeat within an epoch → hard fail (methodology S1)

checks.name: Population & epoch size (G-BIND)
checks.asserts: Bets, seeds, epochs and per-phase counts equal constants in src/, every epoch has exactly epochSize bets, and the dataset's own meta counts are not the denominator.

checks.name: Client-seed influence & Phase D recomputation
checks.asserts: A wrong client seed changes the result at the rate the result lattice predicts (0 % change → hard fail), an empty-seed control is run, every Phase D bet with a player-set seed recomputes, predictable Phase D seeds are disclosed with the exposed epochs enumerated, and the A–C client-seed generator is disclosed and is a CSPRNG.
checks.floor: Client seed not used in computation → hard fail (methodology S2); Phase D ≥ 2 distinct client seeds
checks.declarationTruth: no record labelled phase D when declared 0

checks.name: Result recomputation
checks.asserts: Every bet with a revealed seed recomputes to the recorded result multiplier exactly on the declared result lattice (its decimals, its floor clamp and its cap clamp) under the declared RNG; coverage equals expectedBets; a skipped bet is a FAIL, not an exclusion. A tolerance on a lattice value is a defect: the lattice is the comparison.
checks.floor: Every bet individually recomputed; a single mismatch is a hard fail

checks.name: Draw bias bound
checks.asserts: The draw is exactly uniform on its domain or biased by no more than 2^-32, stated as a computed bound in the step detail: for rejection sampling, MAX_FAIR is a whole number of ranges and the rejection census is printed; for a direct 32-bit draw with no range reduction, the domain is stated as the full 2^32 and the bound is 0 by construction; for a float draw, the float→result mapping is enumerated and the per-target win-probability deviation it causes is printed (rules.drawBias, R1).
checks.floor: Modulo bias exceeding 1/2^32 without rejection sampling → hard fail (methodology S2)

checks.name: RNG reference vectors
checks.asserts: Unit tests reproduce at least one captured bet from its revealed seed and fixed vectors against the operator’s published algorithm or an operator verifier response; the adapter cites the operator source line it ports.

checks.name: Result range & win rule
checks.asserts: Every recomputed result lies inside the declared result range [floor, cap] on its declared lattice, and the recorded win flag equals the declared win rule (≥ or >, against the chosen target or against a declared edge-adjusted threshold) applied to the recomputed result for every bet; no served win flag or result field is read while deriving it, so a served flag that disagrees with the rule is caught.

checks.name: Payout arithmetic
checks.asserts: payout = amount × multiplier for every winning bet and 0 for every loss, compared exactly on the declared money grid (or the declared settlement rule) when one exists, otherwise within an absolute tolerance no looser than 1e-8. The tolerance is read from the declaration.
checks.floor: Payout arithmetic error exceeding 1e-8 → hard fail (methodology S3)

checks.name: Bet-size invariance (Phase C)
checks.asserts: Every elevated-stake bet recomputes identically and is priced and paid by the same rule as a base-stake bet at the same target (same result function, same win rule, same win chance for the target); Phase C is played at a target with a high enough win chance that ≥ 100 elevated-stake wins exercise the payout path, not only the result.
checks.floor: Phase C ≥ 100 bets at elevated stake
checks.declarationTruth: no record labelled phase C when declared 0

checks.name: Payout multiplier & edge placement provenance
checks.asserts: The multiplier paid on every win equals the declared payout rule (the chosen target, exactly, on its declared precision); where the house edge enters — the result formula’s numerator, a scale factor on the result, or the backend win threshold — is declared with its origin (published fairness page, vendored operator source, operator client bundle, or operator config + capture); and any operator-reported win-chance or edge field is compared with the declared formula, never read by the derivation.

checks.name: Target bounds & maximum payout
checks.asserts: Every chosen target lies on the declared target precision within the declared [minTarget, maxTarget]; the result cap and the maximum-payout / exposure clip are declared (or declared undeclared); an advertised maximum target that no legal stake can play, or a client-side target ceiling the server does not enforce, is disclosed; a violation is disclosed, not failed (rules.maxPayout, R2).

checks.name: Target coverage
checks.asserts: Phase A covers the declared target space — the minimum legal target, every decade from 1× up to the highest decade the capture plan declares, and (where the operator has one) targets on both sides of a client-side cap the server accepts — asserted against the capture plan in code rather than described in prose; the number of distinct targets and the decades reached are printed.
checks.floor: All declared target decades; Phase A ≥ 50 bets per decade the plan declares

checks.name: Wallet / balance reconciliation
checks.asserts: When the capture carries a balance field, every consecutive-bet delta equals payout − amount exactly or belongs to a structurally recognised deferred-credit pair; when it carries wallet credit fields instead, those settle by the same rule as the game credit; otherwise the step prints n/a — declared.
checks.declarationTruth: no running-balance-ledger key (a per-bet wallet balance before/after) on any bet record when declared null; per-bet settle amounts declared in money.walletFields (e.g. stakeWallet, winningAmountWallet) and status flags (e.g. balanceOk, walletOk) are not a balance ledger and do not count

checks.name: Boundary semantics: tie, result floor & cap
checks.asserts: The tie case (a result exactly equal to the target or threshold), the result floor (the point mass at the minimum result, e.g. 1.00×, and that it loses at every legal target) and the result cap are each witnessed by data or by operator-verifier probes and recorded as evidence with the witness count; a rule asserted from source alone is declared unwitnessed, never passed silently.

checks.name: Anti-circularity (win probability)
checks.asserts: Win probability per target comes from the draw domain and the win rule alone (a closed form checked against an exact count over the draw domain for at least every served target) and never from an operator-supplied win-chance field; a negative control shows a corrupted result is rejected.
checks.floor: Config probabilities diverge from independent computation → hard fail (methodology S4)

checks.name: Effective edge across the legal target grid vs claim
checks.asserts: The effective edge (1 − RTP) is derived in exact arithmetic for EVERY legal target on the declared target grid — not only the captured ones — from the draw domain, the win rule and the payout rule, and compared with the declared claim; the minimum and maximum edge, where they occur, and the count of targets off the claim are printed in full. A target whose derived edge differs from the claim by MORE than the RTP-CLAIM band (rtpClaimRule.band, 0.1 pp) on the target range the RTP-CLAIM rule scores is a FLAG with the magnitude stated, never silently absorbed into prose; a difference inside the band is printed, not flagged. Where the edge is a backend parameter absent from the published formula, it is measured from the capture and the width of the measurement is printed beside the claim.
checks.floor: Every legal target (the whole declared grid), exact arithmetic

rtpClaimRule.enforcedBy: RTP_CLAIM_RULE_ENFORCED in each package's own src/rtp-claim-switch.ts, true since rule 1.2.0. The rule itself is core/rtp-claim.ts, which every package carries as a byte-identical copy (src/rtp-claim.ts); conformance C-13 compares SHA-256s and reports the package's switch value; bin/sync-rtp-claim.mjs re-vendors the rule and creates a missing switch file with false, never overwriting one.
rtpClaimRule.whileNotEnforced: the package computes the full per-setting exact RTP table, commits it (outputs/rtp-claim-table.json, SHA-256 pinned in src/rtp-settings.ts) and prints the rule's outcome as INFO; this check's own policy and every verdict are unchanged. A committed table that no longer equals the run or its pin exits 1 either way (it is evidence, not the claim).
rtpClaimRule.whenEnforced: 1.2.0: an outcome of FAIL (a setting more than the band below the stated figure, house side) is the package verdict RTP FIGURE OVERSTATED, exit 5: a fail until the casino fixes the figure or the paytable, never printed as NOT PROVABLY FAIR and never a Pass, because the draws themselves pass. Verdict and exit come from rtpClaimVerdict (draw fail 1 > INCOMPLETE 3 > RTP FIGURE OVERSTATED 5 > Conditional 2 > Full 0). NO_CLAIM, NOTED and PUBLISHED are never a miss. A committed table that no longer equals the run or its pin is a reproduction failure, exit 1.
rtpClaimRule.text: The casino can publish either (1) a single number ("99% rtp") — every setting has to be within the band of it; or (2) a range ("rtp 98.65–99.07% depending on settings"), anywhere findable, fairness page or rules is fine — every setting has to sit inside it, and the range has to be the real one: bottom = their actual worst setting, top = their actual best (within the band); no "up to 99%", no range wider than reality. Our audit publishes the full per-setting table. 1.1.0: the claim is the figure shown to players, on the game page, fairness page or help page; a game with no shown figure is marked no claim (kind "none", its source naming the game page, the fairness page and the help page and saying "no RTP figure") and still gets its full per-setting table: outcome NO_CLAIM, never a FAIL, no house-side failures. 1.2.0: six places count (game page, fairness page, help page, bet panel, rules, game settings); an edge stated in the game settings counts as stated, no screenshot needed; claims may be per-setting or tiered (each stake tier held to the edge the casino states for it); a zero-edge or promotional line is noted, not tested; a casino that publishes the real per-setting figures is PUBLISHED, but a bare paytable is not.
rtpClaimRule.band: 0.1 pp (RTP_CLAIM_BAND = 0.001 as a fraction of 1). A setting within 0.1 pp of what the casino states passes; past that on the house side is a FAIL; player-favourable never fails. For a range claim the published bottom may not sit more than 0.1 pp below the true worst setting, nor the published top more than 0.1 pp above the true best.
rtpClaimRule.arithmetic: exact rationals (bigint) for every setting, the claim and the band; an RTP a package can only derive numerically (a recursive EV engine, a double convolution) enters as the exact binary value of that double, and the package states the figure's precision.
rtpClaimRule.industryContext: GLI-11 v2.0 §4.4.1(b) requires the minimum RTP to be met "at all times … at the lowest end of a non-linear paytable", naming keno spot combinations; the lab reports the minimum and maximum theoretical payout.

checks.name: Simulation Pass 1 (fresh seeds)
checks.asserts: Uniformity of the draw on its domain (≥ 2,000,000 draws, chi-squared and serial independence at a family-wise level) plus RTP convergence at ≥ 9 targets spanning the low and high decades at ≥ 1,000,000 rounds each, compared with the exact per-target RTP; statistics re-derived in verify from the artifact’s rows, never trusted from its own scalars; the committed experiment is pinned and replayable — census byte-for-byte, derived statistics within the reproduction tolerance (rules.reproduction).
checks.floor: Limbo reading of the 1,000,000-rounds-per-config floor: ≥ 2M uniformity draws + ≥ 1M rounds on each of ≥ 9 targets

checks.name: Simulation Pass 2 (cherry-pick)
checks.asserts: Every revealed seed × 10,000 nonces; early window = the captured nonce range, reference window = the remainder; the statistic is the return of the targets the casino actually served in that epoch (payout-weighted) against the exact per-target mean and variance, with the null computed exactly or from a seeded, re-derivable bootstrap (never an assumed 0.05); every window re-derived in verify; pre-registered one-sided rule; direction split and detection power printed.

checks.name: Live-sample fit
checks.asserts: Captured results fit the declared result distribution P(R ≥ x) (KS on the continuous part, the point mass at the floor counted separately) and show no serial dependence; informational — a sample of a few thousand rounds has little power and never bears the verdict.

checks.name: S5 fairness-integrity matrix
checks.asserts: exploit-testing.md carries the standardized matrix with framework IDs S5-1 … S5-8, each row Pass / Flag / Hard Fail / Not tested — disclosed, tied to a step or a capture.
checks.floor: All tests in the standardized matrix

checks.name: Player-verifier parity
checks.asserts: The site verifier’s derive.js for this casino is generated from (or hash-matched to) the adapter’s computeResult; the package records that hash.
checks.declarationTruth: cite resolves; when published is false the step prints n/a and the limitations register (DICE-30) carries the row

checks.name: Player check path documented
checks.asserts: README states, in order, how a player verifies one of their own bets: where the seed is revealed, which fields to paste, the exact commitment encoding, the result formula and the win rule — using the declaration’s field names.

checks.name: Dataset & config pins
checks.asserts: The live SHA-256 of the dataset (and of any constants file the derivation reads) equals the constant pinned in src/; the verifier aborts on mismatch before any step runs.

checks.name: Artifacts of record
checks.asserts: Every artifact the report quotes is pinned in src/, un-ignored by name in .gitignore, carries no run metadata, is never rewritten by verify (verify writes only to outputs/run/), and every numeric leaf has a declared value domain; the pin asserts the identity of the committed evidence, and byte identity across machines is required only for exact content — dataset, config, seeds, census — while derived statistics are compared at the reproduction tolerance, never by bytes (rules.reproduction) derived from src/.

checks.name: Fresh-clone reproduction
checks.asserts: On a fresh clone, npm ci && npm test prints N/N steps with the Full Pass verdict and exit 0 within the budget, without modifying any pinned artifact; a regeneration (test:full) is written to outputs/run/ and compared with the committed artifacts field by field — integers and strings exact, non-integer numbers within |Δ| ≤ 1e-14 + 1e-12·max(|a|,|b|) or the per-field tolerance a step declares — with the diff and the runtime version recorded in outputs/run/diff.json and nothing beyond tolerance; the step count in README/MANIFEST/verify.ts comments equals the suite; the audit ID is assigned; the runtime is pinned.

checks.name: Mutation battery
checks.asserts: A step-named mutation registry runs in a disposable copy; every scored step has at least one mutation that kills it; declared survivors are tied to limitation IDs; forgery scripts that re-pin the hash they invalidate are included.

checks.name: Disclosure register & evidence appendix
checks.asserts: MANIFEST carries the declared-limitations register with closure evidence, the load-bearing premises with "could the data contradict it?", and evidence.md numbers every exhibit from E01 with its evidential role; no internal QA material ships in the package.

checks.name: Scaling edge (stake- or exposure-dependent edge)
checks.asserts: When the operator’s configuration declares a stake- or exposure-dependent edge (a scaling edge between a floor and a ceiling): the configuration is pinned; the edge actually applied to every bet is recovered exactly from the bet’s own fields (never sampled) and compared with the declared floor and ceiling; the exposure at which scaling engages is stated with whether the capture reached it; an applied edge off the declared floor inside the capture fails rather than being averaged away; and what the configuration does not publish (the schedule between floor and ceiling) is disclosed, not invented. When the declaration says no scaling edge, the operator source or pinned configuration is read to confirm it (declarationTruth).
checks.declarationTruth: no scaling-edge block (or scaling disabled) in the pinned operator config or the vendored operator source, and every bet’s applied edge equals the flat edge, when declared false; a declared null is unknown and never derives n/a
